breaking_changes: Removed the ROCm backend for OpenMOSS on Linux; set backend to vulkan or cuda instead.
Removed the ROCm backend for sd-cpp on Windows; set backend to vulkan or auto instead.
The POST /v1/images/upscale endpoint now requires the 'upscaling' model label; models without it are rejected with a 400 error.

The /api/v1/system-info API now returns AMD GPU names in marketing form (e.g., 'AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (gfx1201)') instead of raw numeric codes; consumers that parse the name field for numeric versions need to adapt.
The release tagging tool no longer accepts --no-sign; omit the flag (now the default) or use --sign for signed tags.

evidence.blockers: AMD GPU hardware is needed to verify the system-info marketing name display (6d0e01f), and the sd-cpp ROCm error path on Windows (d5f154a). A machine with a configured cloud provider is needed to verify token limit discovery (e8000b4). The release tagging tool needs dry-run verification before the v2026.41 tag (6deeb05).
evidence.breaking_changes: Five breaking changes ship: OpenMOSS and sd-cpp ROCm backends removed (migration to vulkan/cuda or auto documented in backend docs and README), the upscaling endpoint now enforces an 'upscaling' model label, the /api/v1/system-info name field now returns AMD GPU marketing names instead of numeric codes, and the release tagging tool no longer accepts --no-sign.
evidence.coverage: 31 commit reviews span the full range from v2026.39.1 to 6f8e87bbec (head SHA), covering all PRs merged into release-v2026.41. CI passed on every reviewed merge commit across build, test, smoke, docs, CodeQL, and platform packaging workflows.
evidence.manual_testing: Exercise the /api/v1/system-info endpoint on AMD hardware to confirm marketing names. Drive POST /v1/images/upscale with both labeled and unlabeled models. Start an OpenMOSS config on AMD with backend vulkan or cuda. Call GET /v1/models with a cloud provider to check max_output_tokens and max_completion_tokens. Launch Junie on native Windows. Verify the sd-cpp ROCm error on Windows. Validate tray --spawn-server lifecycle on Linux and macOS.
evidence.security: No security concerns observed across the 31 reviewed commits. Config validation tightening (a2e042d) and the watchdog pipe (3b5ec50) are defensive improvements. The ROCm removals (e5d0eec, d5f154a) reduce code and asset surface.
